feed.title: Be Careful With Coca-Cola Right Now

While claims related to products purchased directly from Apple or other retailers were rejected, the tribunal found claims concerning Apple products bought through Amazon's marketplace to be "plausible, credible and grounded in the facts," potentially valuing the case between Â£289 million and Â£306 million.

feed.title: TikTok reaches first state settlement over teen safety claims
feed.summary: TikTok has reached its first state settlement with Alabama over claims that the platform endangered children and misled consumers about its safety. The agreement mandates new usage limits and enhanced age verification for Alabama users, including a two-hour daily time limit and pauses after 15 minutes of use. TikTok will pay Alabama at least $100 million, potentially rising to $300 million if other states join similar agreements.

feed.title: Russian Strikes on Ukrainian Data Centers Leave 100,000 Households Without Internet
feed.summary: Russian forces have broadened their attacks in Ukraine to include data centers and internet providers, resulting in four deaths and leaving approximately 100,000 households without internet access. This campaign targets critical digital infrastructure, raising questions about the legality of striking dual-use facilities that house both military and civilian services. Ukrainian officials emphasize the network's resilience due to its decentralized architecture, though local disruptions and increased costs are anticipated.

feed.title: Apple has been ordered to pay a record $5.7 billion in a case concerning a patent for haptic feedback technology
feed.summary: A U.S. jury has ordered Apple to pay California-based company Taction over $5.7 billion for infringing two patents related to haptic feedback technology used in the iPhone and Apple Watch. Apple plans to appeal the decision, stating that its Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology and that it does not use Taction's intellectual property. This award marks the largest of its kind in U.S. history.

feed.title: US jury says Apple owes record $5.7 billion in haptic technology patent case
feed.summary: A US jury has ordered Apple to pay San Diego-based Taction over $5.7 billion for infringing two of its patents related to haptic feedback technology used in iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple disputes the verdict, stating its Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, and plans to appeal what is reportedly the largest such verdict to date. Taction, which applies its technology in headphones and gaming headsets, initiated the lawsuit in 2021, a case revived by a federal appeals court after an initial ruling favored Apple.

While Jollybot helps build trust, its customizability and brand risks, as highlighted by controversial memes posted by Meta's chief AI officer, also present unique challenges.
